UA project advisors and public contributions, with the context and source for each
      relationship.
text.T006: Strategic Advisor on Governance and Alignment
text.T007: CPMAI Lead Coach | PMI AI Standards Core Team
text.T008:
Focus: project-management standards, organizational alignment, and the operationalization
        of AI governance.
text.T009:
Connected the UA control-theory framing with CPMAI practices in a public discussion of
        constraints, sensors, roles and governance gates.
text.T014: Professor of Intelligent Systems at the University of Waterloo
text.T015: Focus: control-theoretic research and practical engineering governance.
text.T016:
Shared his Social Responsibility Stack paper in the public discussion of UA under Michael
        Risch’s post, bringing a related control-theoretic perspective into the conversation.
text.T020:
These advisory roles are with the UA project. They do not imply institutional endorsement,
    certification or adoption.
text.T025:
Supported the changed-engineering-object framing, emphasizing boundaries, evidence,
        authority, correction loops and the return of human judgment.
text.T036:
Christophe cited UA in his explanation of agentic-system control. Taller’s public visual
        explainer also draws on UA to connect probability distributions, control signals and
        feedback.
text.T042:
Hosted the Corning Learn-AI-Palooza discussion and publicly reflected on UA’s relevance to
        system-level risks, team behavior, ownership and governance.
text.T047:
Developed a public operational interpretation of UA, connecting control loops to roles such
        as Prompt Steward and Evaluation Owner, evaluation signals and governance practices.
text.T051: Founder · Conflux; co-author of Team Topologies
text.T052:
Reshared Michael Risch’s discussion of my AI governance and control-theory article, quoting
        its framing of governance as bringing business intent back into the system.
text.T056:
He also offered public encouragement for UA’s development in the project’s milestone
        discussion.
text.T059: and contributed two further perspectives to the discussion.
text.T061: First, model-mediated systems may expand the range of problems that software can address, rather than merely replace existing solutions.
text.T062: Second, as foundation models and generic agent infrastructure commoditize, domain- and client-specific control architectures may remain a significant source of differentiation.
text.T063: These perspectives extend the discussion beyond runtime engineering into market opportunities, enterprise capabilities, and long-term competitive advantage.
